doc.title: Retry failed webhook deliveries
doc.tldr: Failed deliveries now retry with capped exponential backoff, and operators can see and replay the ones that give up.

risk.why: Changes the delivery worker's ack path; a bug here drops or duplicates events.

doc.ask: Approve the backoff caps; check the migration is reversible.
doc.overview: Before this change a failed delivery was `nack`ed straight back onto the queue and a cron job re-sent everything from the last hour every 5 minutes. Now the consumer hands failures to a **retry scheduler** that uses the queue's delayed publish, and deliveries that exhaust their retries become visible (and replayable) to operators. Read the scheduler first: everything else hangs off it.

sections.title: Retry scheduler
sections.summary: A new `retry` package decides *when* a failed delivery is tried again: capped exponential backoff with jitter, 12 retries over roughly 9 hours, then give up.

blocks.md:
The scheduler is stateless. It computes the next delay from the attempt number carried in the message and publishes a **delayed copy** to the same queue. No polling loop, no extra table to scan, and a restart loses nothing because the delayed message lives in the broker.

| attempt | delay (before jitter) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 30 s |
| 2 | 1 m |
| 4 | 4 m |
| 8 | 1 h (cap) |
| 12 | 1 h, then give up |

blocks.caption: One failed delivery, end to end.
blocks.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Q as Delivery queue
  participant C as Consumer
  participant D as Destination
  participant R as Retry scheduler
  Q->>C: deliver (attempt n)
  C->>D: POST event
  D-->>C: 503
  C->>R: Schedule(delivery)
  alt retries left
    R->>Q: PublishAt(attempt n+1, now + backoff)
    C->>Q: ack original
  else exhausted
    C->>C: MarkFailed
    C->>Q: ack original
  end

blocks.md: **Backoff caps:** 30 s base, 1 h max delay, 12 retries (~9 h). Stripe retries for ~3 days; we stop the same day so a dead endpoint stops costing us. Open for discussion, see the question below.

questions.q: Are 12 retries over ~9 hours the right default?
questions.why: Covers a typical deploy or outage window without keeping dead endpoints alive overnight.

notes.note: Holds no state of its own: the attempt number travels in the message.
PublishAt is the broker's delayed publish (RabbitMQ delayed-message plugin / SQS DelaySeconds).
Replay keeps the attempt counter, so a replayed delivery that fails again gives up immediately.

sections.title: Delivery consumer: the ack path
sections.summary: The consumer no longer `nack`s failures back onto the queue; it schedules a retry and acks the original **only after** the retry is safely queued.

blocks.md: This is the riskiest part of the change. Order matters: *schedule, then ack*. If the process dies between the two, the original is redelivered and the destination sees a **duplicate** attempt. The reverse order would **drop** the event. Duplicates are acceptable (deliveries carry an idempotency key); drops are not.

blocks.caption: Delivery states after this change.
blocks.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pending
  pending --> delivered: 2xx
  pending --> retrying: error, retries left
  retrying --> pending: backoff elapsed
  pending --> failed: error, exhausted
  failed --> pending: operator replay
  delivered --> [*]

notes.note: Schedule first, ack after: a crash here means a duplicate, never a drop.
If the broker refuses the delayed publish we nack, which falls back to the old immediate-redelivery behaviour.
MarkFailed is best-effort like Insert: worst case the delivery is missing from the Failed page, not lost.

sections.title: Rollout
sections.summary: Ship behind the existing `retries_v2` flag, tenant by tenant; the legacy cron stays off once the flag is on.

steps.title: Enable for everyone, delete the cron
steps.detail: The cron code is already removed in this PR; the flag only gates the new path.

sections.title: Remove the legacy retry cron
sections.summary: The every-5-minutes cron that blindly re-sent the last hour of failures is deleted.

blocks.md: It had no backoff and no cap, and it raced with the consumer: an event could be in flight and re-sent by the cron at the same time.

sections.title: Lockfile, generated code, docs rename
sections.summary: `amqp091-go` bump for delayed publish, regenerated OpenAPI types, and the retries doc renamed and updated.

questions.q: Are 12 retries over ~9 hours the right default?
questions.why: Covers a typical deploy or outage window without keeping dead endpoints alive overnight.

questions.q: Should replay reset the attempt counter?
questions.why: A replay is one manual attempt; resetting would silently restart 9 hours of retries.
